source.text: Μετὰ ταῦτα εἶδον, καὶ ἰδοὺ θύρα ἠνεῳγμένη ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, καὶ ἡ φωνὴ ἡ πρώτη ἣν ἤκουσα ὡς σάλπιγγος λαλούσης μετ’ ἐμοῦ, λέγων· Ἀνάβα ὧδε, καὶ δείξω σοι ἃ δεῖ γενέσθαι.

records.literal_gloss: After these things I saw, and behold a door having been opened in the heaven, and the voice the first which I heard as of a trumpet speaking with me, saying: Come up here, and I will show you what things must happen.

en.L: After these things I looked, and look, a door standing open in heaven, and the first voice that I had heard, like a trumpet speaking with me, saying, "Come up here, and I will show you what must take place."
en.B: After this I looked, and there in heaven was a door standing open. The voice I had heard at first, the one like a trumpet that spoke with me, said, "Come up here, and I will show you what must happen."
en.R: Later I looked, and I saw a door standing open in heaven. Then I heard the same voice that had spoken to me before. It sounded like a trumpet. It said, "Come up here. I will show you what must happen."

fr.L: Après ces choses je vis, et voici, une porte ouverte dans le ciel, et la première voix que j’avais entendue, comme [celle] d’une trompette qui parlait avec moi, disant : « Monte ici, et je te montrerai ce qui doit arriver. »
fr.B: Après cela, je regardai, et je vis dans le ciel une porte ouverte. La voix que j’avais entendue la première fois, celle qui ressemblait à une trompette et qui m’avait parlé, me dit : « Monte ici, et je te montrerai ce qui doit arriver. »
fr.R: Plus tard, j’ai regardé, et j’ai vu une porte ouverte dans le ciel. Puis j’ai entendu la même voix qui m’avait parlé avant. Elle résonnait comme une trompette. Elle m’a dit : « Monte ici. Je vais te montrer ce qui doit arriver. »

es.L: Después de estas cosas miré, y he aquí una puerta abierta en el cielo, y la primera voz que [yo] había oído, como de trompeta que hablaba conmigo, diciendo: «Sube acá, y te mostraré lo que tiene que suceder».
es.B: Después de esto miré, y allí, en el cielo, había una puerta abierta. La voz que yo había oído al principio, la que era como una trompeta y hablaba conmigo, dijo: «Sube aquí, y te mostraré lo que tiene que suceder».
es.R: Más tarde miré, y vi una puerta abierta en el cielo. Entonces oí la misma voz que me había hablado antes. Sonaba como una trompeta. Me dijo: «Sube aquí. Te mostraré lo que tiene que suceder».

sw.L: Baada ya haya nilitazama, na tazama, mlango umefunguliwa mbinguni, na ile sauti ya kwanza niliyokuwa nimeisikia, kama tarumbeta ikizungumza nami, ikasema, "Njoo juu hapa, nikuonyeshe yale ambayo lazima yatokee."
sw.B: Baada ya hayo nilitazama, na huko mbinguni palikuwa na mlango uliokuwa wazi. Ile sauti niliyoisikia mwanzoni, iliyokuwa kama tarumbeta ikizungumza nami, ilisema, "Njoo juu hapa, nikuonyeshe yale ambayo lazima yatokee."
sw.R: Baadaye nilitazama, nikaona mlango uliokuwa wazi mbinguni. Kisha nikasikia sauti ile ile iliyokuwa imezungumza nami hapo kwanza. Ilisikika kama tarumbeta. Ilisema, "Njoo juu hapa. Nitakuonyesha yale ambayo lazima yatokee."

decisions.choice: a door opened in heaven: a way into the vision of God's throne
decisions.reason: The opened door lets John see, and then enter, the place where God reigns. Ezekiel says that the heavens were opened and he saw visions of God (Ezekiel 1:1). The same door-language ties back to the open door of 3:8 and the door of 3:20, though the sense here is different.

decisions.choice: the first voice: the trumpet-like voice of 1:10
decisions.reason: "The first voice" is the one John heard at the start, "a loud voice like a trumpet" (1:10), the voice of the risen Jesus. λέγων, "saying", is masculine though "voice" is feminine: the grammar follows the person speaking, not the word.

decisions.choice: what must happen: Daniel 2:28-29 again
decisions.reason: The words recall 1:1 and 1:19, and through them Daniel 2:28-29. What follows in the book is what God has determined must happen.

decisions.choice: look (L); there ... was (B); I saw (R)
decisions.reason: The style guide does not use "behold". Literal keeps a call to attention; Balanced and Readable turn it into a statement of what John saw.

decisions.choice: John's account in the passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("je vis"), in the passé composé at Readable ("j'ai vu"), as in 1:9; the Greek presents kept at Literal (4:5, 4:8)
decisions.reason: As set in 1:9 for the whole book: written narrative takes the passé simple at Literal and Balanced, and Readable uses the passé composé. Where John describes the vision in the present tense, Literal keeps the present, and Balanced keeps it where the English Balanced does. Speech keeps its own tenses.

decisions.choice: he aquí
decisions.reason: In narrative, where John tells what came into view, Literal renders the Greek pointer word with "he aquí"; where someone speaks to a listener it is "mira" or "{{plural_you:miren|mirad}}". Balanced and Readable leave it out or reword it, as the English does.

source.text: μετὰ ταῦτα εὐθέως ἐγενόμην ἐν πνεύματι· καὶ ἰδοὺ θρόνος ἔκειτο ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, καὶ ἐπὶ τὸν θρόνον καθήμενος, καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ὅμοιος ὁράσει λίθῳ ἰάσπιδι καὶ σαρδίῳ, καὶ ἶρις κυκλόθεν τοῦ θρόνου ὅμοιος ὁράσει σμαραγδίνῳ.

records.literal_gloss: After these things \v 2 immediately I came to be in spirit; and behold a throne was standing in the heaven, and on the throne [one] sitting, \v 3 and the [one] sitting like in appearance to stone jasper and to carnelian, and a rainbow around the throne like in appearance to emerald.

en.L: After these things, \v 2 immediately I came to be in [the] Spirit, and look, a throne stood in heaven, and on the throne [one] seated, \v 3 and the one seated [was] like jasper stone and carnelian in appearance, and around the throne a rainbow like emerald in appearance.
en.B: After this, \v 2 at once I came to be in the Spirit, and I saw a throne standing in heaven, with someone seated on it. \v 3 The one seated there looked like jasper and carnelian, and around the throne was a rainbow that looked like emerald.
en.R: Right after that, \v 2 the Spirit took hold of me. I saw a throne in heaven, and someone was sitting on it. \v 3 The one on the throne shone like precious stones, like jasper and carnelian. A rainbow that looked like a green emerald circled the throne.

fr.L: Après ces choses, \v 2 aussitôt je me trouvai dans l’Esprit ; et voici, un trône était placé dans le ciel, et sur le trône [quelqu’un] assis, \v 3 et celui qui était assis [était] semblable d’aspect à une pierre de jaspe et à la cornaline, et autour du trône, un arc-en-ciel semblable d’aspect à l’émeraude.
fr.B: Après cela, \v 2 aussitôt je me trouvai dans l’Esprit, et je vis un trône dressé dans le ciel, et quelqu’un assis sur ce trône. \v 3 Celui qui y était assis avait l’aspect du jaspe et de la cornaline, et autour du trône il y avait un arc-en-ciel qui avait l’aspect de l’émeraude.
fr.R: Juste après, \v 2 l’Esprit s’est emparé de moi. J’ai vu un trône dans le ciel, et quelqu’un était assis dessus. \v 3 Celui qui était sur le trône brillait comme des pierres précieuses, comme le jaspe et la cornaline. Un arc-en-ciel qui ressemblait à une émeraude verte entourait le trône.

es.L: Después de estas cosas, \v 2 al instante llegué a estar en [el] Espíritu, y he aquí un trono estaba puesto en el cielo, y sobre el trono [uno] sentado, \v 3 y el que estaba sentado [era] semejante en aspecto a una piedra de jaspe y de cornalina, y alrededor del trono un arco iris semejante en aspecto a la esmeralda.
es.B: Después de esto, \v 2 enseguida me encontré en el Espíritu, y vi un trono puesto en el cielo, y a alguien sentado en él. \v 3 El que estaba sentado allí tenía el aspecto del jaspe y de la cornalina, y alrededor del trono había un arco iris que parecía de esmeralda.
es.R: Enseguida, \v 2 el Espíritu se apoderó de mí. Vi un trono en el cielo, y había alguien sentado en él. \v 3 El que estaba sentado en el trono brillaba como piedras preciosas, como el jaspe y la cornalina. Alrededor del trono había un arco iris que parecía una esmeralda verde.

sw.L: Baada ya mambo haya, \v 2 mara moja nilikuwa katika Roho, na tazama, kiti cha enzi kilikuwa kimewekwa mbinguni, na juu ya kiti cha enzi [mmoja] ameketi, \v 3 na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} aliyeketi [alikuwa] kama jiwe la yaspi na akiki kwa sura, na upinde wa mvua kukizunguka kiti cha enzi, kama zumaridi kwa sura.
sw.B: Baada ya hayo, \v 2 mara moja nilikuwa katika Roho, nikaona kiti cha enzi kimewekwa mbinguni, na mmoja ameketi juu yake. \v 3 Yeye aliyeketi hapo alionekana kama yaspi na akiki, na kukizunguka kiti cha enzi kulikuwa na upinde wa mvua ulioonekana kama zumaridi.
sw.R: Mara baada ya hayo, \v 2 Roho akanishika. Niliona kiti cha enzi mbinguni, na mmoja alikuwa ameketi juu yake. \v 3 Yeye aliyeketi juu ya kiti hicho aling'aa kama vito vya thamani, kama yaspi na akiki. Upinde wa mvua uliong'aa kama zumaridi ya kijani ulikizunguka kiti cha enzi.

decisions.choice: "after these things" begins the next sentence
alternatives: "after these things" ends 4:1: "what must happen after these things"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT puts a full stop before μετὰ ταῦτα and takes the words with verse 2: "After these things, immediately I was in the Spirit." Many editions put them at the end of verse 1, as in 1:19, "what is about to happen after these things". The record follows the SBLGNT, so the record begins with the last two words of verse 1. The sense of the passage is not much changed.

decisions.choice: in the Spirit: a new stage of the vision
decisions.reason: John was already "in the Spirit" in 1:10. Here the phrase marks a new vision, in which he is taken up to heaven, as Ezekiel was lifted by the Spirit (Ezekiel 3:12-14; 8:3). See the note on 1:10.

decisions.choice: the throne of God, as Isaiah, Ezekiel and Micaiah saw it
decisions.reason: Isaiah saw the Lord seated on a throne, high and lifted up (Isaiah 6:1), and Micaiah saw the LORD on his throne with the host of heaven around him (1 Kings 22:19). Ezekiel saw above the creatures a throne like sapphire, and around the one seated on it a brightness like the rainbow in the clouds (Ezekiel 1:26-28). John's vision draws on all three.

decisions.choice: God is described only by light and color
decisions.reason: John does not describe the form of the one seated on the throne. He tells only how he appeared, in the light of precious stones. The reverence of the description matches the Old Testament's care in speaking of seeing God (Exodus 33:20; Ezekiel 1:28, "the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD").

decisions.choice: jasper, carnelian and emerald: precious stones, their exact colors uncertain
decisions.reason: Ancient names of stones do not always match modern ones. In Revelation jasper is "clear as crystal" (21:11), so it may be a bright, clear stone; σαρδίῳ was a red stone, probably carnelian; the emerald is green. The rainbow (ἶρις) may be a ring of light around the throne. All three stones appear in the high priest's breastpiece (Exodus 28:17-20) and in the walls of the new Jerusalem (21:19-20).

decisions.choice: carnelian
decisions.reason: σαρδίῳ names a red stone from Sardis. "Carnelian" is its modern name; "sardius" is an older English word few readers know.

decisions.choice: the Spirit took hold of me (R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:10, Readable says what "in the Spirit" means.

decisions.choice: jaspe, cornalina, esmeralda
decisions.reason: The usual modern Spanish names of the stones; "sardio" is an old name few readers would know. Their exact colors are uncertain, as the meaning decision says, and the names do not settle them.

decisions.choice: enseguida
decisions.reason: "Enseguida", written as one word, is the settled Spanish for this adverb at Balanced and Readable; Literal keeps "al instante".

decisions.choice: yaspi, akiki, zumaridi
decisions.reason: The Swahili names of the precious stones; "akiki" is carnelian, a red stone, the sense of the Greek name (m5). The exact colours in ancient use are uncertain, as the meaning decision says.

decisions.choice: mara moja
decisions.reason: "Mara moja" for the Greek "immediately", as settled for the Swahili New Testament.

source.text: καὶ κυκλόθεν τοῦ θρόνου θρόνοι εἴκοσι τέσσαρες, καὶ ἐπὶ τοὺς θρόνους εἴκοσι τέσσαρας πρεσβυτέρους καθημένους περιβεβλημένους ἐν ἱματίοις λευκοῖς, καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτῶν στεφάνους χρυσοῦς.

records.literal_gloss: And around the throne thrones twenty-four, and on the thrones twenty-four elders sitting, having been clothed in garments white, and on the heads of them crowns golden.

en.L: And around the throne [were] twenty-four thrones, and on the thrones twenty-four elders seated, clothed in white garments, and on their heads golden crowns.
en.B: Around the throne stood twenty-four other thrones, and on them sat twenty-four elders, dressed in white, with gold crowns on their heads.
en.R: Around the throne there were twenty-four more thrones. Twenty-four leaders, called elders, sat on them. They wore white clothes and had gold crowns on their heads.

fr.L: Et autour du trône [il y avait] vingt-quatre trônes, et sur les trônes, vingt-quatre anciens assis, revêtus de vêtements blancs, et sur leurs têtes des couronnes d’or.
fr.B: Autour du trône se dressaient vingt-quatre autres trônes, et sur ces trônes étaient assis vingt-quatre anciens, vêtus de blanc, avec des couronnes d’or sur la tête.
fr.R: Autour du trône, il y avait vingt-quatre autres trônes. Vingt-quatre chefs, qu’on appelle les anciens, étaient assis dessus. Ils portaient des vêtements blancs et avaient des couronnes d’or sur la tête.

es.L: Y alrededor del trono [había] veinticuatro tronos, y sobre los tronos, veinticuatro ancianos sentados, vestidos con vestiduras blancas, y sobre sus cabezas coronas de oro.
es.B: Alrededor del trono había otros veinticuatro tronos, y en ellos estaban sentados veinticuatro ancianos, vestidos de blanco, con coronas de oro en la cabeza.
es.R: Alrededor del trono había veinticuatro tronos más. En ellos estaban sentados veinticuatro líderes, llamados ancianos. Llevaban ropa blanca y tenían coronas de oro en la cabeza.

sw.L: Na kukizunguka kiti cha enzi [kulikuwa na] viti vya enzi ishirini na vinne, na juu ya viti hivyo wazee ishirini na wanne wameketi, wamevikwa mavazi meupe, na juu ya vichwa vyao taji za dhahabu.
sw.B: Kukizunguka kiti cha enzi kulikuwa na viti vingine vya enzi ishirini na vinne, na juu yake waliketi wazee ishirini na wanne, wamevaa mavazi meupe, na taji za dhahabu vichwani mwao.
sw.R: Kukizunguka kiti cha enzi kulikuwa na viti vingine vya enzi ishirini na vinne. Viongozi ishirini na wanne, walioitwa wazee, waliketi juu yake. Walivaa mavazi meupe, na walikuwa na taji za dhahabu vichwani mwao.

decisions.choice: the twenty-four elders: heavenly beings who lead the worship and who may represent God's people
alternatives: angels of high rank who form God's council
the people of God of both covenants, twelve tribes and twelve apostles
decisions.reason: The text does not say who they are. They sit on thrones near God, as the members of a heavenly council (compare 1 Kings 22:19; Daniel 7:9). Their white clothes and crowns are promised to the faithful (3:4-5; 2:10), and twenty-four may be twelve and twelve, like the gates and foundations of the new Jerusalem, named after the tribes and the apostles (21:12-14). David also divided the temple priests and singers into twenty-four groups (1 Chronicles 24-25). In 7:13-14 one of the elders speaks to John about the redeemed as a group distinct from the elders themselves.

decisions.choice: gold crowns: the wreaths of victors
decisions.reason: στεφάνους is the victor's or honor wreath (see 2:10), here made of gold. In 4:10 they lay them before the throne.

decisions.choice: a list of things seen
decisions.reason: The sentence has no main verb, and the case of the nouns changes partway through, as if "I saw" were understood. It is a list of what John saw.

decisions.choice: leaders, called elders (R)
decisions.reason: "Elders" in a church today means its leaders. Readable says that these are leaders and keeps the name.

decisions.choice: "les vingt-quatre anciens" (L, B); "vingt-quatre chefs, qu'on appelle les anciens" (R), then "les anciens" (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As the style guide (section 9) has it. "Vieillards" says only old age; "anciens" is the word French uses for the elders of Israel and of the church. Readable first says that they are leaders, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: ancianos (L, B); líderes, llamados ancianos (R)
decisions.reason: "Ancianos" is the settled Spanish word for elders, here heavenly beings who lead the worship. Readable explains it as the English does, keeping the word.

decisions.choice: wazee
decisions.reason: "Wazee" (elders), the plain word, since these are heavenly beings (m1) and not church officers; Readable adds "viongozi" (leaders), as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ ἐκ τοῦ θρόνου ἐκπορεύονται ἀστραπαὶ καὶ φωναὶ καὶ βρονταί· καὶ ἑπτὰ λαμπάδες πυρὸς καιόμεναι ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου, ἅ εἰσιν τὰ ἑπτὰ πνεύματα τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου ὡς θάλασσα ὑαλίνη ὁμοία κρυστάλλῳ.

records.literal_gloss: And out of the throne come out lightnings and voices and thunders; and seven lamps of fire burning before the throne, which are the seven spirits of the God, \v 6 and before the throne as a sea glassy like to crystal.

en.L: And out of the throne come lightnings and voices and thunders, and seven torches of fire [are] burning before the throne, which are the seven spirits of God, \v 6 and before the throne [there is something] like a sea of glass, like crystal.
en.B: Lightning flashes out from the throne, with sounds and thunder. Before the throne seven torches of fire are burning, which are the seven spirits of God, \v 6 and before it lies what looks like a sea of glass, like crystal.
en.R: Lightning flashed from the throne, and there were loud noises and thunder. In front of the throne, seven torches were burning. They are the seven spirits of God. \v 6 Also in front of the throne was something that looked like a sea made of glass. It was as clear as crystal.

fr.L: Et du trône sortent des éclairs et des voix et des tonnerres ; et sept torches de feu brûlent devant le trône, qui sont les sept esprits de Dieu, \v 6 et devant le trône [il y a] comme une mer de verre, semblable à du cristal.
fr.B: Du trône jaillissent des éclairs, des voix et des coups de tonnerre. Devant le trône brûlent sept torches de feu, qui sont les sept esprits de Dieu, \v 6 et devant lui s’étend comme une mer de verre, pareille à du cristal.
fr.R: Des éclairs sortaient du trône, et il y avait de grands bruits et des coups de tonnerre. Devant le trône, sept torches brûlaient. Ce sont les sept esprits de Dieu. \v 6 Devant le trône, il y avait aussi quelque chose qui ressemblait à une mer de verre. C’était transparent comme du cristal.

es.L: Y del trono salen relámpagos y voces y truenos; y siete antorchas de fuego [están] ardiendo delante del trono, que son los siete espíritus de Dios, \v 6 y delante del trono [hay algo] como un mar de vidrio, semejante al cristal.
es.B: Del trono salen relámpagos, con estruendos y truenos. Delante del trono arden siete antorchas de fuego, que son los siete espíritus de Dios, \v 6 y delante de él se extiende algo como un mar de vidrio, semejante al cristal.
es.R: Del trono salían relámpagos, y había ruidos fuertes y truenos. Delante del trono ardían siete antorchas. Son los siete espíritus de Dios. \v 6 También delante del trono había algo que parecía un mar hecho de vidrio. Era transparente como el cristal.

sw.L: Na kutoka katika kiti cha enzi inatoka miale ya umeme na sauti na ngurumo, na mienge saba ya moto inawaka mbele ya kiti cha enzi, ambayo ni roho saba za Mungu, \v 6 na mbele ya kiti cha enzi [kuna kitu] kama bahari ya kioo, kama bilauri.
sw.B: Miale ya umeme inatoka katika kiti cha enzi, pamoja na sauti na ngurumo. Mbele ya kiti cha enzi inawaka mienge saba ya moto, ambayo ni roho saba za Mungu, \v 6 na mbele yake kuna kitu kinachoonekana kama bahari ya kioo, kama bilauri.
sw.R: Umeme ulimulika kutoka katika kiti cha enzi, na kulikuwa na sauti kubwa na ngurumo. Mbele ya kiti cha enzi mienge saba ilikuwa ikiwaka. Mienge hiyo ndiyo roho saba za Mungu. \v 6 Tena mbele ya kiti cha enzi kulikuwa na kitu kilichoonekana kama bahari iliyotengenezwa kwa kioo. Kilikuwa safi kama bilauri.

decisions.choice: lightning, voices and thunder: God's presence at Sinai
decisions.reason: When God came down on Mount Sinai there were thunders and lightnings and the sound of a trumpet (Exodus 19:16-19). φωναὶ, "voices", here means loud sounds or rumblings. The same signs return at turning points of the book (8:5; 11:19; 16:18).

decisions.choice: seven torches that are the seven spirits of God
decisions.reason: See the note on 1:4. Zechariah 4:2-6 joins seven lamps with the work of God's Spirit. λαμπάδες were torches or blazing lamps.

decisions.choice: something like a sea of glass: a vast, clear floor before the throne
alternatives: the temple's great bronze basin, called "the sea"
the waters of chaos, stilled before God
decisions.reason: Ezekiel saw above the creatures an expanse like "awesome crystal" (Ezekiel 1:22), and Exodus 24:10 describes under God's feet "something like a pavement of sapphire, like the very heavens". Solomon's temple had a great basin called "the sea" (1 Kings 7:23). In the Old Testament the sea often stands for the powers of chaos, and here it lies calm before God. In 15:2 the sea of glass is mixed with fire, and the victors stand beside it. John says only that it was "like" a sea.

decisions.choice: torches
decisions.reason: These are flames burning in the open, not lamps on a stand like those of 1:12; "torches" makes the difference clear.

decisions.choice: comes (L); flashes (B); flashed (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek tells the vision in the present tense here. Literal and Balanced keep it; Readable keeps the past tense of a story told.

decisions.choice: antorchas
decisions.reason: The Greek word names an open flame carried or set up to give light, which is a torch, not a lamp with oil; Spanish "antorcha" matches the English "torches".

decisions.choice: mienge
decisions.reason: "Mienge" (torches), open flames, as the English has torches; "taa" would suggest the lamps on the lampstands of chapter 1.

source.text: Καὶ ἐν μέσῳ τοῦ θρόνου καὶ κύκλῳ τοῦ θρόνου τέσσαρα ζῷα γέμοντα ὀφθαλμῶν ἔμπροσθεν καὶ ὄπισθεν·

records.literal_gloss: And in [the] middle of the throne and in circle of the throne four living creatures full of eyes in front and behind;

en.L: And in [the] middle of the throne and around the throne [were] four living creatures full of eyes in front and behind.
en.B: And at the throne's center and all around it were four living beings, full of eyes front and back.
en.R: Close around the throne were four living creatures. They had eyes all over them, in front and in back.

fr.L: Et au milieu du trône et autour du trône [il y avait] quatre êtres vivants remplis d’yeux devant et derrière.
fr.B: Au centre, près du trône, et tout autour de lui, se tenaient quatre êtres vivants, couverts d’yeux devant et derrière.
fr.R: Tout près du trône, autour de lui, il y avait quatre êtres vivants. Ils avaient des yeux partout, devant et derrière.

es.L: Y en medio del trono y alrededor del trono [había] cuatro seres vivientes llenos de ojos por delante y por detrás.
es.B: En el centro del trono y a su alrededor había cuatro seres vivientes, llenos de ojos por delante y por detrás.
es.R: Muy cerca del trono, a su alrededor, había cuatro seres vivientes. Tenían ojos por todas partes, por delante y por detrás.

sw.L: Na katikati ya kiti cha enzi na kukizunguka kiti cha enzi [walikuwa] viumbe hai wanne, wamejaa macho mbele na nyuma.
sw.B: Katikati ya kiti cha enzi na kukizunguka pande zote walikuwa viumbe hai wanne, wamejaa macho mbele na nyuma.
sw.R: Karibu kabisa na kiti cha enzi, pande zote, walikuwa viumbe hai wanne. Walikuwa na macho kila mahali, mbele na nyuma.

decisions.choice: in the middle and around the throne: close by it on each side
alternatives: one in the middle, the others around
beneath the throne, as its bearers
decisions.reason: The exact picture is unclear. The phrase most likely means that the creatures stand at the throne itself, one at each side, close enough to seem part of it. In Ezekiel the living creatures are under the expanse that bears the throne (Ezekiel 1:22-26).

decisions.choice: the living creatures of Ezekiel and the seraphim of Isaiah
decisions.reason: Ezekiel saw four living creatures beside God's throne, with wheels full of eyes all around (Ezekiel 1:5-18; 10:12), and later calls them cherubim (10:20). Isaiah saw seraphim with six wings who cry "Holy, holy, holy" (Isaiah 6:2-3). John's creatures share features of both. Their eyes show that nothing escapes their sight.

decisions.choice: living creatures (L, R); living beings (B)
decisions.reason: ζῷα means a living being. "Beasts" in older English versions suggests wild animals and confuses them with the beast of chapter 13, which is a different word.

decisions.choice: "les quatre êtres vivants" at every level (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As the style guide (section 9) has it. "Animaux" would make them beasts and blur them with the beast of chapter 13, the trap the English avoids with "living creatures"; "êtres vivants" says what the Greek word says. Balanced uses the same phrase, where the English varies it to "living beings".

decisions.choice: seres vivientes
decisions.reason: "Animales" would make them beasts, and the book uses another word for the beast; "seres vivientes" names living beings without deciding their kind, and is used at every level and through the book.

decisions.choice: viumbe hai
decisions.reason: "Viumbe hai" (living creatures) at every level, with the agreement used for living beings ("wanne", "walikuwa"); "wanyama" (animals) would say less than the Greek and could be confused with the beasts of later chapters. The English Balanced "living beings" needs no separate Swahili word.

source.text: καὶ τὸ ζῷον τὸ πρῶτον ὅμοιον λέοντι, καὶ τὸ δεύτερον ζῷον ὅμοιον μόσχῳ, καὶ τὸ τρίτον ζῷον ἔχων τὸ πρόσωπον ὡς ἀνθρώπου, καὶ τὸ τέταρτον ζῷον ὅμοιον ἀετῷ πετομένῳ·

records.literal_gloss: and the living creature the first like to a lion, and the second living creature like to a calf, and the third living creature having the face as of a human, and the fourth living creature like to an eagle flying;

en.L: And the first living creature [was] like a lion, and the second living creature like a calf, and the third living creature had a face as of {{gender:a human|a man}}, and the fourth living creature [was] like a flying eagle.
en.B: The first creature looked like a lion; the second looked like an ox; the third had a face like {{gender:a human face|a man's}}; and the fourth looked like an eagle in flight.
en.R: The first creature looked like a lion. The second looked like a young bull. The third had a face like {{gender:a person's|a man's}} face. The fourth looked like an eagle that was flying.

fr.L: Et le premier être vivant [était] semblable à un lion, et le deuxième être vivant semblable à un veau, et le troisième être vivant avait un visage comme [celui] d’un {{gender:être humain|homme}}, et le quatrième être vivant [était] semblable à un aigle qui vole.
fr.B: Le premier être ressemblait à un lion ; le deuxième ressemblait à un bœuf ; le troisième avait un visage {{gender:humain|d’homme}} ; et le quatrième ressemblait à un aigle en plein vol.
fr.R: Le premier ressemblait à un lion. Le deuxième ressemblait à un jeune taureau. Le troisième avait un visage comme celui d’{{gender:une personne|un homme}}. Le quatrième ressemblait à un aigle en train de voler.

es.L: Y el primer ser viviente [era] semejante a un león, y el segundo ser viviente semejante a un becerro, y el tercer ser viviente tenía el rostro como de {{gender:un ser humano|un hombre}}, y el cuarto ser viviente [era] semejante a un águila que vuela.
es.B: El primer ser viviente parecía un león; el segundo parecía un buey; el tercero tenía un rostro {{gender:humano|de hombre}}; y el cuarto parecía un águila en pleno vuelo.
es.R: El primer ser viviente parecía un león. El segundo parecía un toro joven. El tercero tenía un rostro como el de {{gender:una persona|un hombre}}. El cuarto parecía un águila volando.

sw.L: Na kiumbe hai wa kwanza [alikuwa] kama simba, na kiumbe hai wa pili kama ndama, na kiumbe hai wa tatu alikuwa na uso kama wa mwanadamu, na kiumbe hai wa nne [alikuwa] kama tai anayeruka.
sw.B: Kiumbe wa kwanza alionekana kama simba; wa pili alionekana kama ng'ombe; wa tatu alikuwa na uso kama uso wa mwanadamu; na wa nne alionekana kama tai anayeruka.
sw.R: Kiumbe wa kwanza alionekana kama simba. Wa pili alionekana kama fahali mchanga. Wa tatu alikuwa na uso kama uso wa mtu. Wa nne alionekana kama tai aliyekuwa akiruka.

decisions.choice: four faces from Ezekiel, one to each creature
decisions.reason: Each of Ezekiel's creatures had four faces, of a human, a lion, an ox and an eagle (Ezekiel 1:10). In John's vision each creature has one of them. Together they may stand for the whole of living creation: wild animals, tame animals, humankind and birds. Later Christian writers linked the four with the four Gospels, but the text does not.

decisions.choice: a calf: a young bull or ox
decisions.reason: μόσχῳ is a young bull or calf, the animal Ezekiel calls an ox.

decisions.choice: a human face
decisions.reason: ἀνθρώπου means a human being, not specifically a man.

decisions.choice: calf (L); ox (B); young bull (R)
decisions.reason: Literal gives the word's usual sense; Balanced uses "ox", the animal of Ezekiel 1:10; Readable says what the animal is.

decisions.choice: becerro (L); buey (B); toro joven (R)
decisions.reason: The animal is a young bull or ox. The three levels follow the English steps: Literal the young animal, Balanced the familiar draft ox of Ezekiel's vision, Readable a plain description.

decisions.choice: mwanadamu (L, B); mtu (R), no gender span
decisions.reason: "Mwanadamu" and "mtu" mean a human being, so the English gender span has no Swahili counterpart; "mwanamume" (a male) would narrow the meaning (m3).

source.text: καὶ τὰ τέσσαρα ζῷα, ἓν καθ’ ἓν αὐτῶν ἔχων ἀνὰ πτέρυγας ἕξ, κυκλόθεν καὶ ἔσωθεν γέμουσιν ὀφθαλμῶν· καὶ ἀνάπαυσιν οὐκ ἔχουσιν ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτὸς λέγοντες· Ἅγιος ἅγιος ἅγιος κύριος, ὁ θεός, ὁ παντοκράτωρ, ὁ ἦν καὶ ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος.

records.literal_gloss: And the four living creatures, one by one of them having each wings six, around and within are full of eyes; and rest not they have day and night saying: Holy holy holy Lord the God the Almighty, the [one who] was and the [one] being and the [one] coming.

en.L: And the four living creatures, each one of them having six wings, are full of eyes around and within, and they have no rest day and night, saying, "Holy, holy, holy, Lord God the Almighty, who was and who is and who is coming."
en.B: The four living creatures have six wings apiece and are full of eyes around and within. Without rest, day and night, they say: "Holy, holy, holy, Lord God, the Almighty, the one who was and who is and who is coming."
en.R: Each of the four living creatures had six wings. They were covered with eyes, all around and on the inside too. They never rest, day or night. Always they say, "Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God, the Almighty. He always was, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is coming."

fr.L: Et les quatre êtres vivants, chacun d’eux ayant six ailes, sont remplis d’yeux tout autour et au-dedans, et ils n’ont pas de repos, jour et nuit, disant : « Saint, saint, saint, Seigneur Dieu, le Tout-Puissant, qui était et qui est et qui vient. »
fr.B: Les quatre êtres vivants ont chacun six ailes et sont couverts d’yeux tout autour et au-dedans. Sans repos, jour et nuit, ils disent : « Saint, saint, saint, le Seigneur Dieu, le Tout-Puissant, celui qui était, qui est et qui vient. »
fr.R: Chacun des quatre êtres vivants avait six ailes. Ils étaient couverts d’yeux, tout autour et même à l’intérieur. Ils ne se reposent jamais, ni le jour ni la nuit. Ils disent sans cesse : « Saint, saint, saint est le Seigneur Dieu, le Tout-Puissant. Il a toujours été, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vient. »

es.L: Y los cuatro seres vivientes, teniendo cada uno de ellos seis alas, están llenos de ojos alrededor y por dentro; y no tienen descanso de día ni de noche, diciendo: «Santo, santo, santo, Señor Dios Todopoderoso, el que era y el que es y el que viene».
es.B: Los cuatro seres vivientes tienen seis alas cada uno y están llenos de ojos alrededor y por dentro. Sin descanso, de día y de noche, dicen: «Santo, santo, santo, Señor Dios, el Todopoderoso, el que era, el que es y el que viene».
es.R: Cada uno de los cuatro seres vivientes tenía seis alas. Estaban cubiertos de ojos, alrededor y también por dentro. Nunca descansan, ni de día ni de noche. Siempre dicen: «Santo, santo, santo es el Señor Dios, el Todopoderoso. Él siempre ha sido, es y viene».

sw.L: Na wale viumbe hai wanne, kila mmoja wao akiwa na mabawa sita, wamejaa macho pande zote na ndani, wala hawana pumziko mchana na usiku, wakisema, "Mtakatifu, mtakatifu, mtakatifu, Bwana Mungu Mwenyezi, aliyekuwepo na aliyepo na anayekuja."
sw.B: Viumbe hai hao wanne kila mmoja ana mabawa sita, nao wamejaa macho pande zote na ndani. Mchana na usiku hawapumziki, wakisema: "Mtakatifu, mtakatifu, mtakatifu, Bwana Mungu, Mwenyezi, aliyekuwepo, aliyepo, na anayekuja."
sw.R: Kila mmoja wa viumbe hai hao wanne alikuwa na mabawa sita. Walikuwa wamejaa macho pande zote, hata ndani. Hawapumziki kamwe, mchana wala usiku. Daima wanasema, "Mtakatifu, mtakatifu, mtakatifu ni Bwana Mungu, Mwenyezi. Yeye alikuwepo daima, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} yupo, na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anakuja."

decisions.choice: six wings and "holy, holy, holy": the seraphim of Isaiah 6
decisions.reason: In Isaiah 6:2-3 the seraphim, each with six wings, call to one another, "Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts." Saying a word three times makes it as strong as it can be: God is utterly holy. "Almighty" stands for "of hosts", as in 1:8.

decisions.choice: full of eyes all around and within
decisions.reason: ἔσωθεν means inside or within. It may mean the inner side of the wings or the bodies under them. The point is that the creatures see everything.

decisions.choice: who was and who is and who is coming: the title of 1:4 in a new order
decisions.reason: In 1:4 and 1:8 the order is "who is and who was and who is coming". Here the creatures begin with the past: God has always been, is now, and is coming. The title ends again with his coming, not "who will be".

decisions.choice: no rest day and night: unceasing worship
decisions.reason: The phrase means that their praise never stops. In 14:11 the same words are used of those who worship the beast, who have no rest from torment.

decisions.choice: short sentences (R)
decisions.reason: Readable divides the description into short sentences and makes the title of God a sentence about him.

source.text: καὶ ὅταν δώσουσιν τὰ ζῷα δόξαν καὶ τιμὴν καὶ εὐχαριστίαν τῷ καθημένῳ ἐπὶ τῷ θρόνῳ, τῷ ζῶντι εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, πεσοῦνται οἱ εἴκοσι τέσσαρες πρεσβύτεροι ἐνώπιον τοῦ καθημένου ἐπὶ τοῦ θρόνου, καὶ προσκυνήσουσιν τῷ ζῶντι εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, καὶ βαλοῦσιν τοὺς στεφάνους αὐτῶν ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου, λέγοντες·

records.literal_gloss: And whenever will give the living creatures glory and honor and thanksgiving to the [one] sitting on the throne, to the [one] living into the ages of the ages, \v 10 will fall the twenty-four elders before the [one] sitting on the throne, and they will worship the [one] living into the ages of the ages, and they will throw the crowns of them before the throne, saying:

en.L: And whenever the living creatures give glory and honor and thanks to the one seated on the throne, who lives for the ages of the ages, \v 10 the twenty-four elders will fall down before the one seated on the throne, and will worship the one who lives for the ages of the ages, and will throw their crowns before the throne, saying,
en.B: Each time the living creatures give glory and honor and thanks to the one seated on the throne, who lives forever and ever, \v 10 the twenty-four elders fall down before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and worship the one who lives forever and ever. They throw down their crowns in front of the throne, saying:
en.R: The living creatures give glory, honor, and thanks to the one who sits on the throne and lives forever and ever. \v 10 Each time they do this, the twenty-four elders bow down to the ground before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They worship {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, the one who lives forever and ever. They take off their crowns and lay them down in front of the throne. They say,

fr.L: Et chaque fois que les êtres vivants rendront gloire et honneur et action de grâce à celui qui est assis sur le trône, à celui qui vit pour les siècles des siècles, \v 10 les vingt-quatre anciens tomberont devant celui qui est assis sur le trône, et ils adoreront celui qui vit pour les siècles des siècles, et ils jetteront leurs couronnes devant le trône, en disant :
fr.B: Chaque fois que les êtres vivants rendent gloire, honneur et action de grâce à celui qui est assis sur le trône, à celui qui vit pour toujours et à jamais, \v 10 les vingt-quatre anciens se prosternent devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et adorent celui qui vit pour toujours et à jamais. Ils jettent leurs couronnes devant le trône, en disant :
fr.R: Les êtres vivants rendent gloire et honneur à celui qui est assis sur le trône et qui vit pour toujours et à jamais, et ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} remercient. \v 10 Chaque fois qu’ils le font, les vingt-quatre anciens se prosternent jusqu’à terre devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}adorent, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui vit pour toujours et à jamais. Ils enlèvent leurs couronnes et les déposent devant le trône. Ils disent :

es.L: Y cada vez que los seres vivientes dan gloria y honra y acción de gracias al que está sentado en el trono, al que vive por los siglos de los siglos, \v 10 los veinticuatro ancianos se postrarán delante del que está sentado en el trono, y adorarán al que vive por los siglos de los siglos, y echarán sus coronas delante del trono, diciendo:
es.B: Cada vez que los seres vivientes dan gloria, honra y gracias al que está sentado en el trono, al que vive por los siglos de los siglos, \v 10 los veinticuatro ancianos se postran delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y adoran al que vive por los siglos de los siglos. Echan sus coronas delante del trono y dicen:
es.R: Los seres vivientes dan gloria, honra y gracias al que está sentado en el trono y vive para siempre. \v 10 Cada vez que lo hacen, los veinticuatro ancianos se inclinan hasta el suelo delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Lo adoran, al que vive para siempre. Se quitan las coronas y las ponen delante del trono. Dicen:

sw.L: Na kila mara viumbe hai watakapompa utukufu na heshima na shukrani {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} aliyeketi juu ya kiti cha enzi, anayeishi hata zama za zama, \v 10 wale wazee ishirini na wanne wataanguka mbele ya {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} aliyeketi juu ya kiti cha enzi, nao watamwabudu {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anayeishi hata zama za zama, na watazitupa taji zao mbele ya kiti cha enzi, wakisema,
sw.B: Kila mara viumbe hai wanapompa utukufu, heshima na shukrani yule aliyeketi juu ya kiti cha enzi, anayeishi milele na milele, \v 10 wale wazee ishirini na wanne huanguka mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} na kumwabudu yule anayeishi milele na milele. Huzitupa taji zao mbele ya kiti cha enzi, wakisema:
sw.R: Viumbe hai wanampa utukufu, heshima na shukrani yule anayeketi juu ya kiti cha enzi, anayeishi milele na milele. \v 10 Kila wanapofanya hivyo, wale wazee ishirini na wanne wanasujudu mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Wanamwabudu {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}, anayeishi milele na milele. Wanavua taji zao na kuziweka chini mbele ya kiti cha enzi. Wanasema,

decisions.choice: whenever ... will fall: worship that is repeated again and again
decisions.reason: ὅταν with a future verb describes what happens each time: every time the creatures give praise, the elders bow. The future tenses do not point to one event to come but to worship that goes on.

decisions.choice: the one who lives forever: a title of God from Daniel
decisions.reason: Nebuchadnezzar praised "the one who lives forever" (Daniel 4:34), and the angel in Daniel 12:7 swears by him. Revelation repeats it (10:6; 15:7).

decisions.choice: casting crowns before the throne: the homage of lesser rulers
decisions.reason: Kings who submitted to a greater king laid their crowns before him. The elders give back to God the crowns they wear, owning that their honor comes from him.

decisions.choice: for the ages of the ages (L); forever and ever (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:6 and 1:18, Literal keeps the Greek idiom and Balanced and Readable use the English one.

decisions.choice: huanguka ... huzitupa (B)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the Swahili habitual "hu-" for worship that happens again and again (m1); Literal keeps the Greek future.

source.text: Ἄξιος εἶ, ὁ κύριος καὶ ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν, λαβεῖν τὴν δόξαν καὶ τὴν τιμὴν καὶ τὴν δύναμιν, ὅτι σὺ ἔκτισας τὰ πάντα, καὶ διὰ τὸ θέλημά σου ἦσαν καὶ ἐκτίσθησαν.

records.literal_gloss: Worthy you are, the Lord and the God of us, to receive the glory and the honor and the power, because you created all things, and because of the will of you they were and were created.

en.L: "Worthy are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, our Lord and God, to receive the glory and the honor and the power, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} created all things, and because of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} will they existed and were created."
en.B: "Our Lord and God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are worthy to receive the glory, the honor, and the power, because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} created all things: because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} willed it, they existed and were created."
en.R: "Our Lord and God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} deserve to receive glory and honor and power. You made everything that exists. Everything was made and lives because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} wanted it to be."

fr.L: « Tu es digne, notre Seigneur et Dieu, de recevoir la gloire et l’honneur et la puissance, car {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as créé toutes choses, et à cause de {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} volonté elles existaient et ont été créées. »
fr.B: « Notre Seigneur et Dieu, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es digne de recevoir la gloire, l’honneur et la puissance, car {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as créé toutes choses : c’est parce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} l’as voulu qu’elles ont existé et qu’elles ont été créées. »
fr.R: « Notre Seigneur et Dieu, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} mérites de recevoir la gloire, l’honneur et la puissance. C’est {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} qui as fait tout ce qui existe. Tout a été fait et tout vit parce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} l’as voulu. »

es.L: «Digno eres, Señor y Dios nuestro, de recibir la gloria y la honra y el poder, porque {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} creaste todas las cosas, y por {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} voluntad existían y fueron creadas».
es.B: «Señor y Dios nuestro, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} eres digno de recibir la gloria, la honra y el poder, porque {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} creaste todas las cosas: porque {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} lo quisiste, existían y fueron creadas».
es.R: «Señor y Dios nuestro, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} mereces recibir la gloria, la honra y el poder. Tú hiciste todo lo que existe. Todo fue hecho y vive porque {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} quisiste que existiera».

sw.L: "Unastahili {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, Bwana wetu na Mungu wetu, kupokea utukufu na heshima na uweza, kwa sababu {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} uliviumba vitu vyote, na kwa sababu ya mapenzi {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} vilikuwepo na viliumbwa."
sw.B: "Bwana wetu na Mungu wetu, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} unastahili kupokea utukufu, heshima na uweza, kwa sababu {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} uliviumba vitu vyote: kwa kuwa ulipenda, vilikuwepo na viliumbwa."
sw.R: "Bwana wetu na Mungu wetu, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} unastahili kupokea utukufu na heshima na uweza. Wewe uliumba kila kitu kilichopo. Vitu vyote viliumbwa na vipo kwa sababu {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ulitaka viwe."

decisions.choice: our Lord and God: a title that only God may bear
decisions.reason: The Roman historian Suetonius says that the emperor Domitian, who ruled from AD 81 to 96, wished to be called "our lord and god". Whether or not Revelation was written in his reign, the elders give the title to the Creator alone.

decisions.choice: they existed and were created: an unusual order
alternatives: they existed in God's purpose and then were created
they came into being, that is, they were created
decisions.reason: One would expect "were created and exist". "They existed" may mean that all things first existed in God's will and then were made; or the two verbs may say the same thing twice, as Hebrew poetry often does. Either way, everything exists because God willed it.

decisions.choice: worthy because he is Creator
decisions.reason: The song gives the reason for worship: God made all things. The next song (5:9-10) praises the Lamb as worthy because he redeemed a people for God.

decisions.choice: you, your: deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: The elders speak to God, so "you" and "your" take the deity pronoun setting, as the style guide requires.

decisions.choice: "tu", "toi", "ta" for God addressed in worship, with the deity_pronoun span (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As the style guide (section 6) says, God is addressed with "tu". Each "tu", "toi", "ton", "ta", "tes" for God or the Lamb carries the span; one at the start of a sentence ("Tu es digne") is written plainly with its capital.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}}
decisions.reason: When God is addressed, the pronouns "tú" and "tu" carry the deity_pronoun span like the third-person ones; at the start of a sentence they are capitalised in any case and written plain.
